denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: The claim points to a prescribing-provider identifier problem.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Verify prescribing/order/referring provider identity, NPI, role, and the exact claim segment.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: Ordering/referring/prescribing provider name; NPI; taxonomy; claim loop/field; DOS.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: Wrong NPI; provider role mismatch; missing identifier; payer provider-file mismatch.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: Correct the affected provider identifier/claim element and resubmit under payer correction rules.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal only if the identifier was correct and adjudication is demonstrably wrong.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: Original ERA; submitted claim; provider order/referral; NPI/enrollment evidence; payer response.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not replace the prescribing provider with another clinician merely to make the claim pass.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: CMS Medicare claim-processing examples use specific provider-identifier RARCs for CARC 16; follow the applicable MAC rule.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Commercial plans may use different provider-file requirements and claim edits.
denial_fingerprints.source_evidence: X12 RARC N31; CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual

denial_fingerprints.code_meaning: Incorrect claim form/format for this service.
denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: The payer indicates the claim was submitted in an incorrect form or format for the service.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Confirm claim type, 837 transaction, bill type/form, service category, and payer submission instructions.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: 837P/837I; CMS-1500/UB-04 equivalent; bill type; POS; payer routing; service type.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: Wrong claim type; institutional/professional mismatch; invalid format; wrong submission channel.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: Resubmit using the required claim type/format; preserve the original rejection/adjudication record.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal only if the submitted claim type was correct and the payer applied the wrong processing rule.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: Original claim; clearinghouse report; payer submission instructions; ERA; corrected claim.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not change clinical codes merely to overcome a claim-format denial.
denial_fingerprints.prevention_control: Claim-type routing rules and clearinghouse validation before submission.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: Medicare claim type requirements are program/MAC-specific; verify current manual instructions.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Commercial claim-format rules vary by plan and network.
denial_fingerprints.source_evidence: X12 RARC N34; CMS ERA/claims framework

denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: An occurrence-span date field is missing, incomplete, or invalid.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Compare the affected date with the source record and the claim's other date fields.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: Occurrence span dates; admission/discharge dates; claim type; service dates.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: Date omission; invalid date order; wrong date field; transcription error.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: Correct the affected date field and submit according to payer correction rules.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal only when the dates were correctly submitted and the payer's interpretation is demonstrably wrong.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: Original claim; medical record/date source; claim image; ERA; corrected claim.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not invent or backfill dates from unrelated encounters.
denial_fingerprints.prevention_control: Automated date validation and cross-field date logic.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: Institutional Medicare claims may use occurrence/occurrence-span reporting rules; follow the applicable MAC manual.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Commercial institutional claim edits may differ.

denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: A procedure-date field is missing, incomplete, or invalid.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Compare procedure date with the operative/procedure record and the billed service line.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: Procedure date; DOS; revenue code; CPT/HCPCS; claim type.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: Wrong date; missing procedure date; date mismatch between claim and record.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: Correct the procedure-date field and resubmit as required.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal only if the procedure date was correctly reported and payer processing is erroneous.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: Procedure note; claim image; ERA; corrected claim; source scheduling/clinical record.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not change the DOS simply to fit a payer edit.
denial_fingerprints.prevention_control: Cross-check procedure dates against source documentation before billing.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: Medicare institutional billing may apply specific procedure-date requirements; verify the MAC manual.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Commercial requirements vary by claim type and payer.
denial_fingerprints.source_evidence: X12 RARC N301; X12 RARC M51 is related to invalid procedure coding

denial_fingerprints.code_meaning: Duplicate adjustment; M86 says payment was already made for the same/similar procedure within the applicable time frame.
denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: The payer sees the billed service as a duplicate or same/similar service already paid.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Locate prior adjudicated claim; compare patient, DOS, code, units, modifiers, provider, site and claim control number.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: Prior claim ID; DOS; CPT/HCPCS; units; modifiers; provider; site; frequency.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: True duplicate; rebill; corrected claim not linked; same/similar limitation.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: If duplicate is true, stop rebilling. If the original claim is wrong, correct the appropriate claim path.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal when the service is distinct and payer duplicate logic is incorrect; prove separate service/encounter/site as applicable.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: Prior ERA/EOB; procedure note; encounter record; claim history; modifier support.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not add modifier 59 solely to defeat a duplicate edit without a valid distinct-service basis.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: CMS examples support M86 with duplicate/same-similar scenarios; exact Medicare logic is service-specific.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Commercial duplicate and same/similar rules vary by plan.
denial_fingerprints.source_evidence: X12 RARC M86; CMS Medicare examples

denial_fingerprints.code_meaning: Payment adjusted because the payer believes another payer may be responsible.
denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: Possible coordination-of-benefits or other-payer responsibility issue.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Check eligibility, other insurance, payer sequencing, prior EOB, and whether the claim was sent to the correct payer.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: COB indicators; other payer ID; coverage dates; subscriber data; prior EOB; crossover data.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: Other insurance primary; stale COB data; wrong payer sequencing; missing primary payment information.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: Resolve payer sequencing/COB and submit to the correct payer or with required primary-payer information.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal when payer responsibility is wrong and documentation proves the correct sequence.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: Eligibility response; insurance card; primary EOB; COB records; payer correspondence.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not repeatedly rebill the same payer without resolving the underlying COB status.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: Medicare COB/MSP has specific BCRC/MAC responsibilities; follow current Medicare MSP rules.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Commercial COB rules and crossover processes are plan-specific.

denial_fingerprints.code_meaning: The time limit for filing has expired.
denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: The payer says the claim arrived after its filing deadline.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Establish DOS, original submission, clearinghouse acceptance, payer receipt/acceptance, applicable filing limit, and exceptions.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: DOS; first submission date; clearinghouse acceptance; payer receipt; claim status; payer policy.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: Late submission; clearinghouse rejection; wrong payer; enrollment delay; exception not documented.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: If an exception applies, resubmit with required proof; otherwise recovery depends on payer contract/policy.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal/reconsider when timely filing can be proven or a recognized exception applies.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: Clearinghouse acceptance; payer acknowledgment; claim status history; exception documentation.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not use claim-creation date as proof of timely filing.
denial_fingerprints.prevention_control: Timely-filing aging and first-pass acceptance monitoring.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: Medicare has defined timely-filing exceptions; verify current CMS/MAC rules.
denial_fingerprints.source_evidence: X12 CARC 29; CMS Medicare timely-filing guidance

denial_fingerprints.code_meaning: Charge exceeds fee schedule, maximum allowable, or contracted/legislated fee arrangement.
denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: The payer priced the service below the submitted charge; this is not automatically a denial or coding error.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Compare billed charge, allowed amount, contract/fee schedule, network/product, CPT/HCPCS and modifiers.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: Charge; allowed amount; contract rate; network; CPT/HCPCS; modifiers; units.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: Normal contractual adjustment; wrong contract; wrong network/product; pricing configuration error.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: Post contractual adjustment when pricing is correct; correct claim/pricing data if payer used the wrong basis.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal when contract/policy supports a different allowance or payer pricing is wrong.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: Contract; fee schedule; participation record; pricing explanation; claim line details.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not appeal simply because billed charges exceed allowed amounts.
denial_fingerprints.prevention_control: Contract-loading audits and allowed-amount variance monitoring.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: Medicare uses applicable payment methodologies rather than commercial contract pricing.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Commercial allowed amounts depend on exact contract/product/network.

denial_fingerprints.code_meaning: Medical-necessity adjustment with N115 indicating the decision was based on an LCD.
denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: The denial/adjustment is tied to a Medicare Local Coverage Determination.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Identify the MAC, LCD, effective date, service, diagnosis/coverage requirements, and documentation supporting the LCD.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: CPT/HCPCS; ICD-10-CM; DOS; MAC; LCD number; article; documentation.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: Diagnosis does not satisfy LCD; frequency/coverage rule not met; documentation insufficient.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: Correct coding/documentation when the claim fails the LCD requirements and rebill if permitted.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal when the service meets the LCD and documentation supports coverage.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: LCD; billing article; medical record; order; test results; relevant claim data.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not treat N115 as an authorization code or assume an LCD is an NCD.
denial_fingerprints.prevention_control: Pre-bill LCD screening for Medicare services subject to local coverage.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: N115 specifically signals an LCD-based decision; check the applicable MAC's current policy.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Commercial plans may have analogous medical policies but N115 itself is a Medicare/X12 signal.
denial_fingerprints.source_evidence: X12 RARC N115; CMS Medicare Coverage Database

denial_fingerprints.code_meaning: Medical-necessity/coverage decision with N386 indicating an NCD basis.
denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: The adjustment is tied to a Medicare National Coverage Determination.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Identify the NCD, effective date, covered indications, exclusions, and documentation supporting the service.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: CPT/HCPCS; ICD-10-CM; DOS; NCD; medical record; ordering provider; documentation.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: Service does not meet NCD coverage conditions; diagnosis/indication mismatch; documentation gap.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: Correct claim data/documentation when appropriate; otherwise use the applicable Medicare appeal path.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal when the service meets NCD requirements and the record supports coverage.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: NCD; Medicare Coverage Database; medical record; order; test results; claim copy.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not substitute an LCD analysis for an NCD requirement.
denial_fingerprints.prevention_control: Pre-bill NCD coverage check for affected services.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: N386 explicitly identifies an NCD-based decision; its definition was modified effective 03/01/2026.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Commercial plans may have their own coverage policies.
denial_fingerprints.source_evidence: X12 RARC N386; CMS Medicare manual; CMS Coverage Database

denial_fingerprints.code_meaning: N104 indicates the claim/service is not payable under the contractor's claims jurisdiction area.
denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: The claim may have been sent to the wrong Medicare contractor/jurisdiction.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Confirm beneficiary/service jurisdiction, MAC assignment, service location, and claim routing.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: Beneficiary location; service facility; POS; MAC jurisdiction; claim type; payer ID.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: Misdirected claim; wrong contractor routing; jurisdiction misunderstanding.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: Route/resubmit to the correct Medicare contractor according to current CMS/MAC instructions.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal only if jurisdiction assignment is correct and the contractor incorrectly rejected a payable claim.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: ERA; claim routing data; CMS/MAC jurisdiction information; beneficiary/service-location evidence.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not change clinical coding merely to make a jurisdiction denial disappear.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: N104 is explicitly Medicare contractor-jurisdiction language; verify the current MAC using CMS resources.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Not a universal commercial-payer rule; commercial plans have their own service areas.
denial_fingerprints.source_evidence: X12 RARC N104; CMS Medicare contractor guidance

denial_fingerprints.code_meaning: CARC 197 indicates authorization/precertification/notification was absent; N210 is an appeal-rights Alert, not the denial reason.
denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: The authorization-related denial may be appealable, but N210 itself does not explain the missing authorization.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Find authorization requirement, request/approval record, dates, units, provider, service, and notification timing.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: Authorization number; request date; approval date; CPT/HCPCS; units; DOS; provider; site.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: No authorization; wrong authorization; expired/insufficient authorization; notification not timely.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: If payer permits corrected claim after authorization resolution, follow its rules; otherwise use the stated reconsideration/appeal process.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: N210 signals that an appeal may be available; use the payer/MAC's actual appeal requirements.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: Authorization approval; reference number; payer correspondence; clinical order; claim; medical necessity support.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not interpret N210 as proof that authorization existed or as a universal authorization code.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: CMS has a defined Medicare example using CARC 197 with N210; exact authorization requirements remain service/MAC-specific.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Commercial authorization rules vary significantly by plan.
denial_fingerprints.source_evidence: X12 RARC N210; CMS SE18010 / Medicare guidance

denial_fingerprints.code_meaning: CARC 198 concerns authorization/precertification/notification limits; N362 means days or units exceed the acceptable maximum.
denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: The billed quantity may exceed the authorized or otherwise payable maximum; N362 is a units/days signal, not an authorization code by itself.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Compare authorized units/days with billed units/days and the payer's benefit/coverage maximum.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: Authorization units; billed units; DOS; frequency; benefit limit; CPT/HCPCS.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: Over-billing units; authorization quantity exceeded; frequency limit; data error.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: Correct units or authorization linkage when the claim is wrong and resubmit under payer rules.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal when the billed quantity is supported and the payer's maximum was applied incorrectly.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: Authorization; clinical documentation; treatment plan; prior claims; unit calculation; payer policy.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not assume N362 means the authorization was absent; it specifically addresses days/units exceeding a maximum.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: CMS examples support N362 as a days/units maximum signal; verify the exact Medicare benefit/authorization rule.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Commercial unit/frequency and authorization rules vary.
denial_fingerprints.source_evidence: X12 RARC N362; CMS Medicare manual examples

denial_fingerprints.code_meaning: CARC 231 indicates mutually exclusive procedures; N628 says an outpatient follow-up visit on the same date as a scheduled test/treatment is disallowed.
denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: The denial may reflect same-day service incompatibility, but N628 should not be treated as a universal CARC 231 pairing.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Check the actual ERA RARC, same-day services, code pair, payer policy, and whether the edit is NCCI or another payer edit.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: CPT/HCPCS pairs; DOS; modifiers; POS; payer policy; NCCI edit status.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: Mutually exclusive code pair; same-day visit/test rule; payer-specific edit.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: Correct coding only when the code combination is wrong; otherwise document distinct services and follow payer appeal/reconsideration.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal when documentation and coding rules support separate payment and the payer applied the wrong edit.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: Claim lines; clinical note; NCCI edit data where applicable; payer policy; modifier support.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not automatically add a modifier to bypass an edit.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: CMS NCCI is a distinct Medicare methodology; confirm the current NCCI edit files rather than relying on RARC text alone.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Commercial plans may adopt NCCI or use proprietary edits.
denial_fingerprints.source_evidence: X12 RARC N628; CMS NCCI FAQ/PTP resources

denial_fingerprints.code_meaning: CARC 236 concerns an NCCI/procedure-modifier incompatibility; N519 says the HCPCS modifiers are invalid in combination.
denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: The modifier combination may be invalid or incompatible with the billed procedure.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Review CPT/HCPCS, every modifier, payer policy, NCCI edit and whether the modifiers are clinically supported.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: CPT/HCPCS; modifiers; DOS; units; POS; NCCI PTP edit; documentation.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: Invalid modifier combination; unsupported modifier; modifier order/usage error.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: Remove/correct only the invalid modifier combination and resubmit according to payer rules.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal when the modifier combination is valid and supported but was incorrectly rejected.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: Claim lines; NCCI edit; CPT guidance; operative/clinical documentation; payer policy.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not add unrelated modifiers simply to override an edit.
denial_fingerprints.prevention_control: Modifier validation and NCCI edit checking before submission.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: CMS states NCCI is a correct-coding program, not medical-necessity or prior-authorization review; check the current edit files.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Commercial plans may adopt NCCI methodologies or use different edits.
denial_fingerprints.source_evidence: X12 RARC N519; CMS NCCI FAQ

denial_fingerprints.code_meaning: CARC 284 indicates an authorization number may be valid but does not apply to the billed services; M62 indicates a missing/incomplete/invalid treatment authorization code.
denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: The authorization information may exist, but the authorization identifier or treatment authorization data does not properly apply to the billed service.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Compare authorization number/type with CPT/HCPCS, DOS, units, provider, site and treatment authorization record.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: Authorization number; service code; units; DOS; provider; facility/site; authorization type.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: Wrong authorization linked; incomplete authorization code; service outside approved scope; provider/site mismatch.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: Correct authorization linkage/data when supported and resubmit per payer rules.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal when the authorization clearly covers the billed service and payer processing is wrong.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: Authorization approval; authorization detail; claim; payer confirmation; treatment plan.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not invent or reuse an authorization number from a different service/date/provider.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: Medicare-specific authorization programs are service-specific; verify the applicable MAC/CMS requirements.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Commercial authorization systems and reference formats vary by payer.

denial_fingerprints.code_meaning: These CARCs indicate attachment/documentation-related adjustment categories.
denial_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: The payer needs a specific missing/invalid document or attachment; the exact action depends on the actual ERA RARC and attachment workflow.
denial_fingerprints.first_60_second_checks: Read the actual RARC and attachment request; identify document type, submission channel, deadline, and whether the payer wants original or corrected claim.
denial_fingerprints.claim_fields_to_inspect: Attachment control number; document type; claim ID; medical record; order; operative/pathology/radiology report; submission channel.
denial_fingerprints.likely_root_causes: Attachment missing; wrong document; incomplete document; attachment not linked; transmission failure.
denial_fingerprints.correction_path: Submit the exact requested document or corrected claim using the payer's approved attachment process.
denial_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal when documentation was timely submitted and the payer failed to associate or review it correctly.
denial_fingerprints.evidence_package: Requested document; transmission confirmation; attachment control number; claim/ERA; payer correspondence.
denial_fingerprints.wrong_fix_warning: Do not upload a generic medical-record packet without identifying what the payer actually requested.
denial_fingerprints.medicare_mac_branch: Medicare attachment requirements are program/MAC-specific; use the actual RARC and current MAC instructions.
denial_fingerprints.commercial_payer_branch: Commercial attachment requirements and portals vary by payer.

payer_intelligence.Correction Route: Corrected/replacement claim; UHC states corrected claims replace the prior submission and use frequency code 7 with original claim reference.
payer_intelligence.Appeal/Reconsideration Route: UHC describes a 2-step process for claim determinations: reconsideration first, then appeal; timing is generally 12 months for the two-step process subject to applicable rules.
payer_intelligence.Important Operational Rule: A rejected claim is not the same as a denied claim; rejected claims did not enter adjudication and should be corrected/resubmitted.
payer_intelligence.Source: UHC 2026 Administrative Guide; UHC Claims/Appeals/EDI pages

payer_intelligence.Market/Scope: Commercial / Medicare / Medicaid products vary by plan
payer_intelligence.Correction Route: Reconsideration covers reimbursement/coding decisions and claims needing reprocessing; some scenarios go directly to appeal.
payer_intelligence.Appeal/Reconsideration Route: Reconsideration generally within 180 days of initial claim decision; appeal generally within 60 days of reconsideration decision, with exceptions by issue/product.
payer_intelligence.Important Operational Rule: Aetna explicitly distinguishes reconsideration from appeal and states some claim types bypass reconsideration.

payer_intelligence.Correction Route: Claim coding-edit issues may be submitted as reconsideration through Cigna for HCP/Provider.Evernorth; routine claim corrections follow payer instructions.
payer_intelligence.Appeal/Reconsideration Route: Cigna has a provider payment appeal process; provider appeals generally must be submitted within 180 calendar days of initial payment/denial notice, subject to law/contract.
payer_intelligence.Important Operational Rule: Cigna may resolve many claim issues through customer service/real-time adjustment before formal appeal.

payer_intelligence.Correction Route: Finalized claim disputes/appeals are supported online through Availity Essentials; participating-provider reconsideration details are in provider manuals.
payer_intelligence.Appeal/Reconsideration Route: Medicare Advantage nonparticipating provider appeals: generally 65 calendar days from denial; commercial provider appeals depend on policy/state rules and representation requirements.
payer_intelligence.Important Operational Rule: Humana warns against duplicate appeal submissions; finalized-claim disputes can be placed in an Availity worklist before submission.
payer_intelligence.Source: Humana Provider Claims Submissions; Reconsiderations & Appeals

payer_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: UHC generally uses a two-step claim dispute path: reconsideration first, then appeal if reconsideration is unfavorable.
payer_fingerprints.first_checks: Confirm the claim was adjudicated; identify denial reason; verify applicable plan/state exception; check filing deadline.
payer_fingerprints.correction_path: Correct claim data first if the claim is actually wrong; otherwise file reconsideration.
payer_fingerprints.appeal_path: If reconsideration is unfavorable, use the appeal step unless the applicable law/plan provides another route.

payer_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: UHC's standard reconsideration process has state-law exceptions, including specified states listed in its 2026 guide.
payer_fingerprints.first_checks: Identify member state, product, network status and whether the dispute is a UM/clinical denial, COB, coverage or payment issue.
payer_fingerprints.correction_path: Follow the state-specific process when the standard route is excluded.
payer_fingerprints.appeal_path: Use the state-required appeal/dispute path when applicable.

payer_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: UHC's medical claim review includes claims without required authorization; the exact authorization requirement remains service/plan specific.
payer_fingerprints.first_checks: Check eligibility, responsible payer, provider contract status, authorization requirement, authorization ID, dates, units and site.
payer_fingerprints.correction_path: If authorization existed but was not linked or claim data is wrong, correct per payer instructions.
payer_fingerprints.appeal_path: If authorization was obtained and covers the service, use the applicable reconsideration/appeal process.

payer_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: Aetna categorizes reimbursement, coding and reprocessing issues as reconsideration in its general dispute framework.
payer_fingerprints.first_checks: Classify the denial before routing; verify initial decision date and plan/state exceptions.
payer_fingerprints.correction_path: Correct claim only if submitted data is wrong; otherwise request reconsideration.

payer_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: Certain adverse initial decisions based on medical necessity, payment policy or experimental/investigational coverage skip reconsideration.
payer_fingerprints.first_checks: Read the denial basis and identify whether it falls into Aetna's direct-to-appeal categories.
payer_fingerprints.correction_path: Only correct actual claim-data errors before appeal.
payer_fingerprints.appeal_path: File the appropriate appeal with the required documentation.

payer_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: Aetna's general 180-day dispute standard has numerous fully-insured state exceptions.
payer_fingerprints.first_checks: Identify member state, product funding, provider status, dispute type and initial decision/payment date.
payer_fingerprints.correction_path: Use the applicable state/product deadline and route.
payer_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal/reconsider within the correct state-specific window.

payer_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: Cigna directs coding-edit denials to reconsideration when the claim was denied/not processed as expected because of coding edits.
payer_fingerprints.first_checks: Identify exact edit, code pair, modifier, documentation requirement and whether a claim-service-center adjustment is available.
payer_fingerprints.correction_path: Correct coding only when incorrect; otherwise request reconsideration.
payer_fingerprints.appeal_path: Use provider appeal when the reimbursement decision remains disputed after available claim review.
payer_fingerprints.source: Cigna Appeals and Disputes; Cigna Submit Claims

payer_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: For Cigna COB situations, the timely-filing calculation can use the primary carrier's EOB/EOP processing date.
payer_fingerprints.first_checks: Confirm Cigna is secondary; locate primary processing date; verify whether claim was originally timely to primary.
payer_fingerprints.correction_path: Submit COB information under the applicable exception/routing rule.
payer_fingerprints.appeal_path: Appeal if evidence proves the COB deadline was calculated incorrectly.

payer_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: Cigna says many issues, including timely filing, incomplete claims and contract/fee-schedule disputes, may be resolved through customer service/real-time adjustment.
payer_fingerprints.first_checks: Contact payer/claim service center first where the issue is administrative and potentially correctable.
payer_fingerprints.correction_path: Provide requested information or correct claim when permitted.
payer_fingerprints.appeal_path: Use formal appeal if the issue cannot be resolved and remains appealable.

payer_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: Humana supports online disputes/appeals for finalized Medicare, Medicaid and commercial claims through Availity Essentials.
payer_fingerprints.first_checks: Confirm claim is finalized; locate claim in Availity; determine dispute/appeal type.
payer_fingerprints.correction_path: Correct claim if data is wrong; otherwise use finalized-claim dispute workflow.
payer_fingerprints.appeal_path: Submit through the applicable Humana appeal/dispute route.

payer_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: Humana commercial provider appeals have representation/state-law considerations and use policy/state timelines rather than one universal provider deadline.
payer_fingerprints.first_checks: Determine whether provider is appealing on behalf of member or under independent provider rights; check state law and policy.
payer_fingerprints.correction_path: Correct claim if appropriate; otherwise file appeal under the applicable representation/right.
payer_fingerprints.appeal_path: Use Humana's commercial appeal process and applicable state/product rules.

payer_fingerprints.practical_diagnosis: BCBSIL provides electronic claim review/reconsideration for certain finalized commercial claim denials, while clinical appeals follow a separate route.
payer_fingerprints.first_checks: Confirm BCBSIL plan and whether denial is administrative/payment or clinical.
payer_fingerprints.correction_path: Use corrected claim when data is wrong; otherwise route to claim review or clinical appeal.
payer_fingerprints.appeal_path: Use clinical/provider appeal when the denial basis requires that route.
